name: glm47_mla_decode_grouped_h20_ckv512_kpe64
description: GLM-4.7-Flash absorbed-MLA grouped decode attention, page_size 1. One query token per sequence attends over that sequence's pages in the paged KV pool; the pool row is 576 wide (512 compressed KV + 64 rope key) and the value tensor is the same row truncated to 512, which is why the capture recorded v_buffer with stride 576. Shapes, page tables and split counts come from GLM-4.7-Flash served with its own SGLang cookbook command on 8x B300 (GSM8K 0.820 on the capture run).

num_seqs.description: Decode batch: one query token per sequence.

qk_head_dim.description: Pool row width: 512 compressed KV + 64 rope key.

kv_lora_rank.description: Compressed-KV width, which is also the value width.

kv_pool_rows.description: Rows in the paged KV pool the server allocated.

max_kv_splits.description: Split-K depth the scratch buffers are sized for.

constraints: v_buffer is k_buffer[..., :kv_lora_rank] - the same storage, not a copy

k_buffer.description: Paged KV pool. The benchmark allocates the recorded geometry and fills only the pages kv_indices names, so the addresses, the strides and the number of distinct pages a sequence walks are the captured ones while the page contents are drawn - the same split the native gdn_prefill task makes between its real cu_seqlens and its drawn q/k/v. The capture recorded which pages this row reads but not their 24 MB of contents.

v_buffer.description: A view of k_buffer truncated to the compressed-KV width (stride qk_head_dim).

o.description: Destination. The kernel writes through it and returns None.

attn_logits.description: Split-K partial accumulator. Written before read.

num_kv_splits.description: Per-sequence split count chosen by the scheduler.

o.description: Attention output, written through the o argument.

reference:
"""Reference for GLM-4.7-Flash MLA grouped decode attention.

Independent of the kernel under test: one sequence at a time, gather the pages this
sequence owns, and run the textbook attention on them in float32. The absorbed-MLA
layout is what makes this short - the same pool row holds the compressed KV and the
rope key, so `k_buffer[i]` is the full 576-wide key and `v_buffer[i]` is its first 512
columns.
"""

import torch


@torch.no_grad()
def run(
    q,
    k_buffer,
    v_buffer,
    o,
    kv_indptr,
    kv_indices,
    attn_logits,
    attn_lse,
    num_kv_splits,
    max_kv_splits,
    sm_scale_withk,
    v_scale,
    logit_cap=0.0,
    sinks=None,
    xai_temperature_len=-1,
    has_mla=False,
    use_pdl=False,
    page_size=1,
    score_mod=None,
    aux_tensors=None,
):
    num_seqs = q.shape[0]
    for seq in range(num_seqs):
        start = int(kv_indptr[seq].item())
        end = int(kv_indptr[seq + 1].item())
        if end <= start:
            # A sequence with no cached history attends to nothing. Softmax over an
            # empty axis is NaN, so the answer is a zero row, not a division.
            o[seq].zero_()
            continue
        pages = kv_indices[start:end].long()
        keys = k_buffer[pages].squeeze(1).float()
        values = v_buffer[pages].squeeze(1).float()
        logits = (q[seq].float() @ keys.transpose(0, 1)) * float(sm_scale_withk)
        if logit_cap and logit_cap > 0:
            logits = logit_cap * torch.tanh(logits / logit_cap)
        weights = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        o[seq] = ((weights @ values) * float(v_scale)).to(o.dtype)
    return o
